Subject: Next steps: Isolation model choices & evidence checklist — Cortex Health POC

Hi Anita / Ben —

Thanks again for the demo earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can progress the security & deployment qualification for the POC:

1) Compliance posture (questions)
- SOC 2: please confirm current Type (I vs II) and expected Type II completion date. Do you accept a vendor SOC 2 from subservice orgs, or do you require Redwood to be listed directly?
- HIPAA: you mentioned PHI in the POC. Please confirm whether Cortex is a covered entity or business associate and whether a BAA is required for the POC.
- GDPR: any EU-resident data requirements for this POC (data residency / processor agreements)?

2) Deployment isolation options we discussed
- Private VPC with customer VPC peering (preferred for low-latency)
- Customer-managed private deployment (Redwood Private in their VPC)
- On-prem air-gapped option for regulated customers (appliance or airlock export/import)

3) Evidence & artifacts we need from Cortex to scope the architecture
- Network diagram showing ingress/egress, NAT/gateway, and any on-prem connections (attach if available)
- Inventory of data types touched by the POC (PHI, PII, etc.)
- List of security contacts and SSO/KMS owners

4) Redwood deliverables we propose
- Completed vendor security questionnaire (attached) — draft to you by July 6
- Draft private-deploy architecture diagram for your environment — by July 3
- Deep-dive with infra & security to validate routing and KMS integration — propose July 2 or 5 (30–60 min)

Attachments: redwood_vendor_questionnaire.pdf (application/pdf) — please confirm preferred format and any extra fields you need.

Would you confirm the SOC 2 timing and whether Cortex requires a BAA? Also, share the network sketch if you have one handy — that will let us pick the cleanest isolation model.

Thanks,
Lauren

Subject: Re: Next steps: Isolation model choices & evidence checklist — Cortex Health POC

Thanks Lauren — useful summary. A few clarifications from our side:

- SOC 2: Cortex completed a SOC 2 Type I in Jan 2027 and is tracking to complete Type II by 2028-10-15. For initial POC work we can accept vendor attestation and a controls mapping; for production purchases we will need Type II (expected date above).
- HIPAA: Cortex is a covered entity; we will need a signed BAA before any PHI goes into a vendor environment. For the POC we can scope out a reduced dataset that avoids PHI while we get the BAA in place.
- GDPR: not in scope for this initial POC (data will remain US-resident). We do have EU customers elsewhere and will re-evaluate for EU POCs.

I've attached a quick network sketch (cortex_network_sketch.png) that shows our on-prem VPN concentrator and the cloud VPC we use for staging. The sketch is high level — we'll follow up with a more formal diagram if needed.

Security contact: security@cortexhealth.com (please copy for all questionnaire exchanges).

Happy to meet July 2 at 10:00am PT for the infra deep dive.

Ben

Director, IT Infrastructure

All — quick ops note and suggested owners so we have clear SLAs on deliverables:

Action items (proposed)
- Redwood: complete and return vendor security questionnaire (lauren owner) — due 2028-07-06
- Redwood Infra: produce private-deploy architecture sketch that overlays with Cortex network sketch (karthik owner) — due 2028-07-03
- Cortex: provide formal network diagram and list of required outbound egress destinations for the POC (Ben / security) — target 2028-07-05
- Legal: BAA draft (if PHI is in scope) — Cortex legal + Redwood legal sync (TBD)

Technical notes:
- Based on Ben's sketch, the least-invasive path for low-latency is a customer VPC peering / private link into a Redwood Private deployment. That lets Cortex control VPC routing and KMS, while we run the inference runtime in customer-managed subnets.
- If Cortex needs a fully air-gapped option, we can propose an export/import airlock flow. That has higher operational burden and is typically reserved for customers with strict data egress controls.
- For HIPAA, we will need a BAA and confirmation which datasets are PHI. For initial POC we recommend a synthetic or de-identified sample until the BAA is signed.

I'll prepare a short checklist for the infra call (routing table entries, peering ASN, KMS key alias expectations, required service endpoints). Karthik — can you capture that checklist and share before the July 2 call?

Thanks,
Marissa

Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
